questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How buttons on clothes were invented
Why people fear clowns
Why we find buttons so tempting to push
How to design safer fire alarms
questions.why: They discuss buttons and, with Professor Connor, why buttons are so appealing to us.

questions.q: According to Professor Steven Connor, why are some buttons put high up on the wall?
options: To keep them away from children
To make them easier to see
To save space
To protect them from water
questions.why: He says buttons have to be kept away from children, so they're put high up on the wall.

questions.q: What does Professor Connor say about buttons that really matter?
options: They should be brightly coloured
They should be hard to push, for example behind glass
They should always be at a height that is easy for everyone to reach
They should only be used by adults
questions.why: He says important buttons 'have to be made quite hard to push – like put behind glass'.

questions.q: What does Neil say about himself as a child?
options: He was afraid of buttons
He never noticed buttons
He once broke a fire alarm by pressing it
He loved pressing any button he saw
questions.why: Neil says he loved pressing buttons as a child and would press any that he saw.

questions.q: Why do everyday buttons, like lift buttons, need to be convenient?
options: They have a useful, practical purpose
Because they are expensive to replace when broken
Because children like them
Because they are often dangerous
questions.why: Neil says many buttons have a practical purpose, so they must be easy to use.

questions.q: What is Professor Connor's explanation for why we like buttons?
options: We enjoy the noise they make
We want to feel in control of the machines around us
We have an instinct to fidget and adjust things
We are addicted to technology
questions.why: He says it's 'down to the fidgeting instinct' of creatures with fingers.

questions.q: When Professor Connor calls humans 'digital creatures', what does he mean?
options: We spend a lot of our time online using computers
We are good with numbers
We like modern technology
We have fingers and like to use them
questions.why: Neil explains a digit is a finger or toe, so we are creatures with fingers.

questions.q: Why does Professor Connor mention apes?
options: To say apes also enjoy pressing buttons
To compare our fidgeting with their grooming
To explain where the English word 'button' originally comes from
To show that apes are afraid of buttons
questions.why: He links our wish to fidget and adjust things to 'the grooming instinct in apes'.
